messages.author: 467324c7303934a0
messages.subject: figures: separating code (inline) and figure(s) (float)
parts:
I'm revising a legacy Sweave vignette to use knitr, after running Sweave2knitr() on the .Rnw file.

Under Sweave, in order to have the text and code for a figure appear inline, but the generated figures appear in a
float, I resorted to doing things manually, e.g., generating the figure in a chunk, then writing an explicit
\begin{figure} ... \end{figure} using \includegraphics{}.  Otherwise, if I included the chunk within the
figure environment, the code would appear in the float.

Is there some way to clean this up in knitr?  i.e., use knitr features to achieve this?
One problem is that I often have long figure captions,
and knitr requires that the <<*>>= stuff be all on one line.

An earlier post by Frank Harrell seemed to imply that he had created some customizations for these
purposes, but that is fairly old
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/knitr/includegraphics|sort:date/knitr/bYj3Zn11hjE/1SYK9k8iv7sJ


Here is an excerpt from the file:

<<include=FALSE>>=
opts_chunk$set(engine='R',fig.height=6,fig.width=7,results='hide',fig.show='hide',echo=TRUE)
opts_chunk$set(fig.path='fig/vcd-tut-')
opts_chunk$set(tidy=FALSE)
@

...


The resulting \code{ca} object can be plotted just by running the \codefun{plot}
method on the \code{ca} object, giving the result in
\figref{fig:ca-haireye}.  \codefun{plot.ca} does not allow labels for dimensions;
these can be added with \codefun{title}.
It can be seen that most of the association is accounted for by the ordering
of both hair color and eye color along Dimension 1, a dark to light dimension.
<<ca-haireye,echo=TRUE,fig.keep='high'>>=
plot(ca(HairEye), main="Hair Color and Eye Color")
title(xlab="Dim 1 (89.4%)", ylab="Dim 2 (9.5%)")
@

\begin{figure}[htb]
\begin{center}
%<<ca-haireye,results='hide',echo=FALSE>>=
%plot(ca(HairEye), main="Hair Color and Eye Color")
%title(xlab="Dim 1 (89.4%)", ylab="Dim 2 (9.5%)")
%@
\includegraphics[width=0.7\textwidth]{fig/vcd-tut-ca-haireye}
\caption{Correspondence analysis plot for the \data{HairEye} data.}
\label{fig:ca-haireye}
\end{center}
\end{figure}

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] figures: separating code (inline) and figure(s) (float)
parts:
Hi Michael,

Very good question. That should be easy, and this feature has been
there since knitr v0.9 (Jan 2013), although I did not promote it
particularly. See example 103 at
https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples

I do not see a good reason for fig.show='hide'. I think it is bad to
do that and manually \includegraphics{} later, because you have to
worry about figure filenames, e.g. when you change the chunk label,
you will have to manually update the filename accordingly.

I agree that it is cumbersome to write a long caption (fig.cap="....")
in a chunk header in one line, and that is one motivation for the
document hook hook_movecode(). Other chunk options should be short and
easy to write, e.g. fig.align="center" (so that you do not have to
\begin{center}\end{center})

Since I have finished the knitr book in LaTeX, I'm relatively
confident that most LaTeX headache/problems that you can think of have
probably been solved. Maybe I should start writing checks of $2.56 for
the rest of problems? :)

Regards,
Yihui

parts:
Hi Yihui

Thanks for the example.  I actually discovered the document hook, hook_movecode()
only on p. 154 of your new book. 

I'm surprised that this is not more visible or featured
in documentation, since this seems to be a more natural way to write -- i.e., include
the code for figures, just once, in a chunk within the figure environment, but have the code printed
inline, rather than within the float.

best,
-Michael
